How I work

Every project here
started as a complaint.

Not a brief. Someone on the team was losing hours to something that shouldn't take hours, or budget was going somewhere it shouldn't. The work was noticing it — then finding what actually fixed it.

Step one

Name the real problem

Not "we need more leads." Closer to: we lose leads between midnight and nine because nobody is awake to answer them.

Step two

Test the options honestly

Start with the free, obvious tool. Push it until it breaks, and understand exactly why it broke before paying for anything.

Step three

Build it, then watch it

Ship a version that works this week, not a perfect one next quarter. Then sit with real traffic and see where it leaks.

Step four

Keep tuning

Every question the system couldn't answer becomes the next update. That's how it goes from working to reliable.

Case two

Paid Media Midpoint Travel Jul — Dec 2024

Good ads pointed at
a page that wasn't ready

The problem

Everything went into Google Ads, and every ad sent people to a website that wasn't in shape to convert them. The campaigns weren't the weak link — the destination was. We were paying full price for clicks and losing them on arrival.

The honest fix would have been rebuilding the site, and that wasn't going to happen quickly. So I stopped sending paid traffic to it in the meantime: pulled the website link out of the ads and routed people to the hotline instead, where a person could actually close them. Then I went back through the titles, descriptions and keyword sets and rewrote them properly. By the midpoint of my time there, the account was consistently holding a top-3 position on search ads for our target keywords.

Case three

AI Automation Travel Sawa · Amr Badawy · ElGala Tours Jul 2025 — Present

The inbox that
never closed

The problem

Two of us covered mornings, two covered evenings, and it still wasn't enough. During a campaign launch the comments and DMs came in faster than anyone could type. And nobody worked midnight to nine — so every shift opened with a night's worth of unanswered messages already waiting. The real cost wasn't the replies. It was that a designer and a content creator were spending most of their shift answering DMs instead of making the work they were hired to make.

  1. Meta Business Suite automation

    The free built-in option — obvious first step. It couldn't scope a keyword trigger to a single post. We run many trips across different departments at once, so any trigger fired on every post on the page simultaneously.

    Failed — no per-post control
  2. Keyword-in-caption workaround

    Next idea: ask people to comment the destination name — "Georgia", "Iceland" — so the right trigger fired. It held while things were quiet. Under real campaign traffic, people ignored the instruction. Reviewing threads later, we found comments that had never been answered at all. Leads lost.

    Failed — broke under real traffic
  3. ManyChat

    Answers every comment regardless of what the person typed, sends trip details, asks for the number, and writes name and number straight into a Google Sheet for sales. Anything genuinely off-script gets answered by a human — then I update the flow so it won't be off-script next time. Recorded leads went up immediately. Stable within one week, enhanced throughout the first month.

    Adopted — stable in one week
  4. WhatsApp API on the same system

    An IT colleague had spent a month trying to build an AI support chatbot for WhatsApp and hadn't got it working. I suggested a simpler route: convert the number to WhatsApp API and connect it to the ManyChat flows we already trusted. It collects name and trip code, sends details, captures the lead into the same sheet, and offers "talk to a person" — which notifies whoever's available. Because every reply carries a website link, it lifted site traffic too.

    Built in days — not a month

How the system works.

What the data showed. The most useful thing the system told us had nothing to do with speed — it proved which traffic channel actually converts.

Organic · 90 days
Clicks15.7K
Conversations started14.0K · 89.5%
Leads captured1.3K
Paid · 90 days
Clicks127.6K
Conversations started13.9K · 10.9%
Leads captured616
The insight

Paid brought eight times more clicks and produced half the leads. An organic click was roughly eight times likelier to turn into a real conversation. The automation didn't just save the team's hours — it proved which channel was worth the money.
